best_prompt:
Produce exactly one concise, information-dense caption (one grammatical sentence) describing only visibly present facts. Follow this ordered checklist and include each item only if clearly visible; omit any field you cannot verify:

- 1) Exact count(s) using numerals (e.g., "3 people") and arrangement with left/center/right or foreground/midground/background.
- 2) Main subject(s) and precise action naming specific body/vehicle parts involved (e.g., "pushing bicycle by the handlebars," "rear wheel lifted," "holding puppet by right hand").
- 3) Salient object descriptors: colors, materials, and distinctive accessories (e.g., "red bag on right handlebar," "chrome frame," "striped shirt").
- 4) One short camera viewpoint token (e.g., "wide shot," "high-angle," "close-up").
- 5) One short lighting/shadow token (e.g., "backlit," "long shadow to left," "spotlight").
- 6) One background landmark or surface texture (e.g., "cracked salt flat," "red-tiled roof," "draped blue tent").

Use concrete positional language (left/center/right, foreground/midground/background). Do not use vague quantifiers ("several," "some," "a group"), do not infer relationships, motivations, emotions, or use metaphors; state only what is directly visible. Keep the sentence concise and information-dense, following the approximate order: count + subject + action/part + descriptors + viewpoint + lighting + background.
final_prompt:
Produce exactly one concise, information‑dense caption: a single grammatical sentence of comma‑separated short phrases. Output only that one sentence and nothing else.

Output slots (emit in this order; slots 1–3 are mandatory and must be preserved if they contain MEDIUM/HIGH verified tokens):
1) Subject token (0–3 subject groups) plus one chosen anchor/prop token (see deterministic anchor priority below).
2) Micro‑action / contact (always emit one, see Micro‑action rules).
3) Fine class (verified label or dataset token); if not MEDIUM/HIGH verified, use the safe plural fallback "people/dogs/vehicles/vendor stand".
4) Clothing / clear pose / orientation — include only when MEDIUM/HIGH verified.
5) Up to two anchors/signage (only if MEDIUM/HIGH verified; otherwise use neutral positional anchors such as "storefront behind", "marquee above").
6) Spatial/cropping/depth token if MEDIUM/HIGH verified.

Deterministic anchor priority (select the highest available and place it early):
- 1st: OCR text (use full quoted text if OCR_conf ≥ 0.85; else one short quoted token ≤6 chars only if 0.50 ≤ OCR_conf < 0.85 AND saliency_score ≥ threshold).
- 2nd: large prop/signage (largest segmented area or flagged prop).
- 3rd: people/faces (detected fine class).
- 4th: distinctive color/clothing patch.
Place the chosen anchor within the first 6–8 words together with the subject token. If no MEDIUM/HIGH anchor exists, use a neutral anchor and still place it within the first 8 words.

Verification gating (use provided detector/OCR/motion outputs with these actionable if/elif rules):
- OCR_HIGH: OCR_conf ≥ 0.85 → emit full quoted text and placement phrase (e.g., "on wall left").
- OCR_MED: 0.50 ≤ OCR_conf < 0.85 AND saliency_score ≥ threshold → emit one short quoted token (≤6 chars) and placement.
- Otherwise → do not emit text; use neutral positional anchor.
- SEGMENTATION_HIGH: segmentation_iou ≥ 0.75 (treat as HIGH verification).
- SEGMENTATION_MED: 0.40 ≤ segmentation_iou < 0.75 (treat as MEDIUM verification).
- COUNT_DIGITS: emit digits only if detector_count_confidence ≥ 0.70; otherwise use plural nouns. If detector strongly indicates zero, you may emit "none".

Micro‑action rules (always emit one; pick the highest evidence template available):
- HIGH evidence (use when part segmentation or motion_confidence ≥ 0.85): exact form "left|right [hand|foot|part] [strong‑verb] [object]" (e.g., "right hand holding basket").
- MEDIUM evidence (use when segmentation_iou ≥ 0.40 OR detector_confidence ≥ 0.70): pick one verb from whitelist {jumping, pawing, clearing, showing, speaking, holding, carrying, pushing, pulling, strumming, leaning}. You may append a short orientation token ("back view", "seen from behind") when MEDIUM verifies orientation.
- LOW evidence (fallback): "[part] near [object]" (e.g., "right hand near object").
Never omit or hedge this slot.

Fine class and clothing:
- Emit fine class or clothing only when verified at MEDIUM/HIGH. If not verified, use the safe plural fallback. MEDIUM whitelist tokens (boat, canoe, shrine/temple, ghats/steps, children, performer, vendor, vendor stand, parade participant, marquee, boats, canopies, flagpole, ladder, bicycle, hedgerow, trees, "navy sweater", "red patterned dress", "white blouse") may be emitted only when MEDIUM verification applies and only in their designated slot.

OCR and signage specifics:
- If emitting OCR text, always include a short placement phrase (e.g., "on wall left", "above the doorway"). Do not invent, complete, or guess partial text. If OCR_MED has low saliency, revert to a neutral anchor.

First‑words rule and deterministic minimal rewrite:
- Within the first 8 words, include the subject token (or plural fallback) and the chosen anchor token (OCR token if selected, otherwise prop/people/color anchor). If this cannot be satisfied, auto‑rewrite to this minimal safe caption exactly (use this template and nothing else):
  "group of people, storefront behind, right hand near object, people/dogs/vehicles/vendor stand."
(This minimal template is the deterministic fallback to ensure a valid single sentence when requirements fail.)

Pruning and length control:
- Target: 10–16 words. Hard cap: 22 words. Allow +2 words beyond target when a HIGH anchor is present or when BOTH a MEDIUM anchor and a MEDIUM micro‑action are present.
- Prune deterministically in this order until within caps:
  1) Compress adjective chains (e.g., "large red metal" → "large red metal" compacted).
  2) Remove lighting/reflection descriptors.
  3) Remove object state/material descriptors.
  4) Remove background/ancillary context.
- Never prune tokens used to satisfy verification rules (OCR quoted text, MEDIUM/HIGH anchors, verified counts) in slots 1–3.

Counts and numerals:
- Emit exact digits only when detector_count_confidence ≥ 0.70. Otherwise use plural nouns; do not use vague quantifiers like "several" or "a few". If detector indicates zero with high confidence, emit "none".

Anti‑hallucination absolutes (do not do these):
- Do not invent brand names, complete partial text, invent ages, emotions, intentions, or unsupported attributes.
- No hedging language or speculative words (may, maybe, possibly, appears to be).
- If a detail is not verified at MEDIUM/HIGH, replace it with an approved neutral fallback (e.g., "storefront behind", "marquee above", "object on table", "group of people").

Final validator (must pass before emitting caption):
- One grammatical sentence of comma‑separated short phrases.
- First 6–8 words include subject token (or plural fallback) and chosen anchor (or neutral anchor).
- Micro‑action slot present and follows the templates above.
- Length within caps and pruning rules applied.
- No hedges, no invented text/brands, no duplicated phrases.
- Only allowed MEDIUM tokens are used under MEDIUM verification.
- If any check fails, emit the deterministic minimal safe caption given above.

Succinct exemplars (ideal outputs for reference):
- OCR_HIGH example: "group of people, right hand holding 'Le Mignon' sign on wall left, storefront behind."
- PROP_MED example: "woman, right hand holding red shopping bag, storefront behind, marquee above."
- PEOPLE_MED example: "two people, back view sitting on bench, black tufted bench foreground, floor reflections."
- LOW evidence example: "group of people, right hand near object, people/dogs/vehicles/vendor stand."

Adhere strictly to these rules and emit only the single final caption sentence.

best_record.feedback_instruction:
You are evaluating a captioning prompt for a frozen image captioning model.
The prompt is used to generate captions for images.
The primary objective is to improve CLIP image-text similarity.
SigLIP is reported only as a secondary diagnostic metric.

This is multimodal feedback mode.
For each low-performing example, an image-grounded critique is provided.
Use the aggregate scores and critiques to provide concise, critical feedback on how the prompt should be changed.
Do not produce captions for the examples.
Do not suggest external rerankers, verifiers, multiple candidates, tags, JSON, or non-caption protocols.

Aggregate score report:

- image_id: flickr30k_test_016410
  image_relpath: images/flickr30k/flickr30k_test_016410.jpg
  caption: Shredding the dirt: A shirtless biker leans into a daring BMX trick, muscles taut and wheels airborne against a backdrop of green hills and clear blue sky.
  clip_score: 0.321564
  delta_clip: -0.000000
  image_grounded_critique:
    - Ask the captioner to describe the stunt more precisely: specify which wheel is touching the ground vs. airborne (e.g., front-wheel balance/nose manual vs. rear wheel lifted) instead of generic phrases like "wheels airborne."
    - Require inclusion of distinctive background landmarks and setting (grassy embankment, dirt track, nearby water and the large circular structure/Ferris-wheel–like arch) to better anchor the scene.
    - Encourage noting salient apparel and bike details (shirtless rider with backward cap, ripped jeans, visible tattoo; chrome BMX frame and red rim/peg) and the strong backlighting/high‑contrast lighting to increase discriminative cues.
- image_id: flickr30k_test_024370
  image_relpath: images/flickr30k/flickr30k_test_024370.jpg
  caption: A sunny day in a European city, with a grand, tree-lined street flanked by classic architecture and pedestrians strolling along the sidewalks.
  clip_score: 0.264559

    - Ask the captioner to record prominent vegetation and framing: specify the two large leafy trees centered in front that partially obscure the facade and the elevated vantage point looking down across the street.

  image_relpath: images/flickr30k/flickr30k_test_003863.jpg
  caption: Five friends leap joyfully in unison over a vast, cracked salt flat, arms raised as they chase a yellow ball under a clear blue sky.
  clip_score: 0.345549

    - Require explicit mention of any airborne object and its position (e.g., "a yellow ball mid-air above the center") rather than implying actions like "chase" that may be wrong.

best_record.textgrad_loss_text:
I won’t produce a caption for the image. Instead, based on the aggregate metrics and the image-grounded critiques, here are concise, actionable changes to the global captioning prompt to improve CLIP image–text alignment (focus on adding discriminative, verifiable visual detail and avoiding vague language).

Recommended prompt additions and edits (add as explicit rules in the global prompt):

1. Favor literal, verifiable detail; avoid metaphors, emotive language, guesses about relationships or intent (e.g., don’t assume “friends” or “chasing” unless clearly shown).

2. Always state exact counts for visible people/animals/major objects and their arrangement (e.g., “three people in a horizontal line, left-to-right”). Replace group labels with counts unless a role is visually obvious.

3. Describe precise actions and the physical parts involved (use specific verbs): e.g., “pushing the bicycle by the handlebars,” “riding with rear wheel lifted,” “jumping with both feet off ground.” If a part is interacting (front/rear wheel, right hand), name it.

4. Report colors, materials, and distinctive object details for salient items: clothing colors and styles, accessories (hats, bags), bike/frame/rim color, brick vs. stone facades, roof color, visible tattoos, etc.

5. Anchor scene with concrete background landmarks and setting elements: trees, embankment, crosswalk, fences, tent drapes, arches, water, Ferris-wheel–like structures. Use positional language (foreground/midground/background; left/center/right).

6. Specify camera viewpoint and shot type when visible: high-angle / low-angle / overhead / close-up / wide shot; mention if viewpoint looks down, up, or level with subjects.

7. Describe lighting and shadow cues: backlit/rim light, long shadows, hard sunlight, high contrast, spotlight, overcast. State direction of major cast shadows when visible.

8. Mention notable small objects and their relative positions (e.g., “yellow ball mid-air above center,” “red bag on handlebars, right side”). Indicate if objects are airborne and where relative to people.

9. Describe ground and surface texture when informative (e.g., cracked salt flat, dirt track, paved crosswalk) and any empty or open horizon lines.

10. Prefer concrete architectural details over region labels: number of stories, window shape/arrangement, façade material, roof type/color, visible ornamentation.

11. Avoid vague quantifiers and generics: replace “several,” “some,” “a group,” “wheels airborne,” “a European city,” with specific counts, parts, and descriptors.

12. Keep captions concise but information-dense: one sentence is fine—prioritize discriminative nouns/adjectives (objects, colors, counts, positions, actions, viewpoint, lighting). Do not pad with stylistic flourishes.

13. Add an explicit rule: only assert what is visually present; do not infer unseen relationships or motivations.

How to integrate into prompt text (short template lines to insert):
- “Include: exact counts + left/center/right arrangement; precise action verbs and which body/vehicle part is involved; object colors/materials; one-line camera viewpoint; one-line lighting/shadow cue; one-line background landmark. Avoid speculation and metaphors.”

These changes force captions to include discriminative, verifiable tokens (counts, colors, parts, positions, textures, viewpoint, lighting, unique landmarks) that improve CLIP alignment while reducing generic or speculative phrasing.
